Green industrialization is not just about scaling renewables. It is about rebuilding one of the largest energy-consuming systems in the global economy — where industry accounts for 30% of global energy use, yet still relies on fossil fuels for more than 60% of it.

Yesterday, I participated in the "Building from the Belém Declaration on Global Green Industrialization — First Full Meeting of Supporting Countries and Organizations", organized by UNIDO and the Brazilian government ahead of the International Vienna Energy and Climate Forum (IVECF) . With $1 trillion in industrial decarbonization projects in the pipeline but few reaching final investment decision, three opportunities stood out:

	1.	Align energy, industry, and trade strategies. Green industrialization is becoming a source of competitive advantage. The global clean energy market could grow from $1.2 trillion to $3 trillion by 2035.

	2.	Integrate digital systems and AI into decisions. AI alone could reduce energy sector emissions by 1.3–2.6 Gt CO2 annually — equivalent to the EU's total emissions today.

	3.	Coordinate infrastructure, policy, and finance. The constraint is no longer capital. With financing costs up to 7x higher in key markets, system alignment will determine where the next generation of industry is built.

Green industrialization is now a question of system design. The countries that move first to align demand, infrastructure, and finance will not only decarbonize, they will shape the next phase of industrial growth.
